1.x: **Agra (1504):** founded by **Sikandar Lodi** and made the capital.
**Gulrukhi:** pen name of **Sikandar Lodi**, who wrote **Persian poetry**.
**Tax on grains:** abolished by **Sikandar Lodi**, with several taxes and trade restrictions.
**Portuguese arrival:** **Vasco da Gama, 1498** – Delhi ruler **Sikandar Lodi**.
**Background:** **Nizam Khan**, third son of Bahlol; crowned **17 July 1489**; **greatest Lodi**.
**Rule:** from **Punjab to Bihar**; took **Jaunpur**; beat **Bengal** rulers and **Rajput** chiefs.
**Gaz-i-Sikandari:** yard to **measure land** (used later by Sher Shah and Akbar); audits and **spies**; punished embezzlement.
**Religion:** broke images at **Jwalamukhi (Nagarkot)**, destroyed **Mathura** temples, imposed **jizya** – yet had a **Sanskrit medical work translated into Persian**.
**Buildings:** **Moth ki Masjid** (by his minister); royal tombs of the **Lodi Gardens** (double dome).

2.x: **Timur (Taimur / Tamerlane):** 14th-century Turkish conqueror; born 1336 at Kesh; claimed descent from Chengiz.
**Year:** **1398**; crossed the **Indus** (30 Sept 1398) → **Multan, Bhatnair** → sacked Delhi for three days (**December 1398**).
**Sultan at the time:** **Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah Tughlaq** (also printed "Nasiruddin Mohammad Tughlaq"), the last Tughlaq.
**Dynasty after Timur:** the **Sayyids** (Khizr Khan, 1414); the Tughlaqs lingered only to 1412-14.
**Effects:** Tughlaq state broke into regional kingdoms (**Jaunpur, Malwa, Gujarat**); the Mughal Empire came later (Babur, 1526).

r: Founder and **first Lodi Sultan**; Governor of Punjab (Sirhind, Lahore); throne from Alam Shah; conquered **Jaunpur**; longest reign; Bahlul coin
Son of Bahlol; Agra, Gaz-i-Sikandari, Gulrukhi
Son of Sikandar; arrogant to nobles; killed at Panipat; **last Lodi ruler and last Delhi Sultan**

3.x: **Order of the Afghan rulers:** **Bahlol → Sikandar → Ibrahim**.
**Lodis:** **First Afghan** dynasty; Sultan = "**first among equals**" among Afghan nobles.
**Revolt:** Nobles plotted to enthrone his brother **Jalal Khan**; Ibrahim seized **Gwalior** (which sheltered Jalal) and made **Vikramajit** a vassal.

5.x: **Khizr Khan:** Timur's governor of Multan / **viceroy**; arrested **Daulat Khan Lodi**, took Delhi **1414**; ruled as a deputy **without the title of Sultan**; **accepted the suzerainty of Timur's son Shah Rukh**.
**Mubarak Shah:** failed against the **Khokhars**; **Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi** by **Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi**; octagonal tomb with **blue enamelled tiles** and **guldasta** motifs.
**End:** **Alam Shah voluntarily** gave the throne to **Bahlol Lodi** (1451) – the only Sultan to abdicate.
